title: Use an existing hollow
hook: Socks beside the shoe or inside it. How much packed volume do they add inside?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a shoe already encloses empty space, so socks stuffed inside it add nothing to the packed volume while socks beside it do

misconception: Socks take up the same room in a bag wherever you pack them.
objective: A shoe is hollow: in this model it has 600 cm³ of empty space inside. Socks that fit in that space add nothing to what you pack. Only socks bigger than the space spill over and add volume.

recall.question: A shoe has a 500 cm³ hollow inside its outline. You have 300 cm³ of rolled socks. In the ideal model, how much outer volume do they add if packed inside it?
recall.why: In the ideal hollow model, socks that fit within the existing hollow add max(0, 300 − 500) = 0 cm³ outside. Packed beside the shoe they add all 300 cm³. Use clean, dry items and do not force the shoe.
